It should resist reduction by the sulfide and oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2. Li2ZrF6 (penalty 0.099) was the closest tetravalent analog, and Ti4+ is smaller and may reduce the ZrF4/PF5-type products. Its sulfide-side penalty is unverified.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electrochemically robust lithium-ion conductor with a phosphate network that is largely inert toward both LiCoO2 at 4.0 V and sulfide electrolytes. As a thin interlayer it should block electron transfer and limit interfacial decomposition, which is the main purpose of a coating here. Its low-penalty interface is plausible but unverified.

LiCl is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium halide that shares its anion with the Li6PS5Cl electrolyte, so the contact should not drive new anion-exchange or sulfur-oxidation products. Oxide-type coatings like Li3PO4 reacted with the sulfide to form P2O5, SO2 and SCl4 (penalty 0.337 eV/atom). A halide interlayer should avoid that pathway, and it is also oxidation-stable against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) gave an insulating, wide-gap result but a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom from reaction with the sulfide electrolyte, so a different chemistry is needed.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a Li-rich, wide-gap borate with a fully oxidized B(III) center and no P-S or S-Cl bonds to exchange with the sulfide. Its oxide framework may be less prone to the P2O5/SO2 pathway seen with Li3PO4, and it is a different chemical family from the phosphate and halide coatings tried so far. Its stability against sulfide and LiCoO2 at 4.0 V is unverified.
